title: Drag ghost shows green (would-validate) even when no snap target exists
detail: valid == .None doubles as 'legal target' and 'no target' (drag_to == 0). Dragging over empty space or back over the source renders the green ghost_ok line although nothing would validate — the comment's promise is false mid-drag.
recommended_fix: Introduce a distinct untargeted state; keep .None only for snapped-legal, and color the ghost neutral/gray until a target snaps.

title: Fiber 'glowing inner core' draws with the same color as the pipe — no glow; palette.json's pipe_core is never read
detail: tier_pipe_color maps wide→pipe_fiber, so the inner 0.45-width line has the identical color to the outer line: visually a no-op. data/palette.json defines a distinct pipe_core glow color that the Palette struct and palette_load never read.
recommended_fix: Add pipe_core to the Palette struct and palette_load (jcol default {122,168,230,255}) and draw the inner core with v.palette.pipe_core.

title: Catalog cross-check omits content_host, yet all three seed_fixture copies spawn it ignoring the lookup's ok
detail: A catalog missing content_host makes node_type_index return (0,false); the ignored ok spawns node_types[0] (residential) at the host position via topology_spawn_node's unchecked index. Deterministic but silently wrong; only the two enforced types are protected.
recommended_fix: Require content_host in catalogs_load's cross-checks, and/or make seed_fixture propagate the ok and abort when a required type is missing.

title: draw_text truncates UTF-8 runes to u8 — the em dash in the window title renders as a garbage byte
evidence:
+	cbuf := make([dynamic]u8, 0, len(txt)+1, context.temp_allocator)
+	for c in txt {
+		append(&cbuf, u8(c))
+	}
+	append(&cbuf, 0)
+	rl.DrawText(cstring(raw_data(cbuf)), x, y, size, col)
...
+	title := "Packet Plumber — v2 story 1.2"
detail: for c in txt iterates runes; u8(c) keeps only the low byte, so the multi-byte em dash (U+2014) becomes one invalid byte. The HUD title, the app's first visible text, renders garbled.
recommended_fix: Encode runes as UTF-8 (utf8_encode / core:utf8) before DrawText, or drop non-ASCII characters from the title.

title: W1 drift-check's six mutations never exercise the validation-failure class that step.odin's replay_error latch exists for
detail: All six mutations fail at parse/header level inside log_read. None produces a header-valid, parse-valid log whose command fails topology validation (unknown/dead node id, self-loop, over-span) — precisely the class step.odin's replay_error latch detects. That latch path is never tested.
recommended_fix: Add a seventh mutation that flips a command payload field (e.g. a node id) so the log parses but fails validate_draw, and assert the gate rejects it.

title: diff.patch is truncated — it ends mid-hunk inside run_replay, so the tail of replay_hashes is not reviewable
detail: The patch ends at this line — the remainder of run_replay, and replay_hashes's post-loop return (including whether a latched replay_error forces ok=false), is absent. The gate's rejection semantics cannot be fully verified from this diff.
recommended_fix: Re-emit the complete patch; reviewers need replay_hashes's tail to confirm ok reflects a latched replay_error.

title: CI invokes tools/harness.sh (run + drift-check) but no tools/* file appears in this diff
evidence:
+      - name: Golden harness (T1 hashes + T2 software pixels + replay gate)
+        run: tools/harness.sh run
+
+      # W1 carry-forward from #21: a deliberately-drifted action log must be
+      # REJECTED by the replay gate — proven in CI, not just locally (the
+      # #599-r2 / verification-gap lesson).
+      - name: W1 drift-rejection negative test
+        run: tools/harness.sh drift-check
detail: The replaced 1.1 comment says this path was to 're-enable in story 1.2+', yet this diff adds no tools/harness.sh or rlsw build script. If the script is not already committed, CI fails at the golden-harness step; unverifiable under lens isolation.
recommended_fix: Confirm tools/harness.sh and the rlsw shadow build script are committed with this story; otherwise include them in the PR.

title: Draw_Intent.tier comment promises a 'default standard' the parser never applies
detail: The parser requires all six fields and errors when the tier is absent — no defaulting exists anywhere. The doc comment describes behavior the code does not implement.
recommended_fix: Either drop the 'default' claim from the comment, or default tier to 'standard' when the field is missing.

title: App.res_id / rt_id / host_id are write-only — seeded but never read
evidence:
+	std_tier:  u16, // the tier app draws (the workhorse 'standard')
+	res_id:    u32,
+	rt_id:     u32,
+	host_id:   u32,
...
+	app.res_id, app.rt_id, app.host_id = seed_fixture(&app.state, &cat)
detail: The three ids are assigned from seed_fixture and never referenced again anywhere in the new app/main.odin — input and rendering work from snap results, not these ids. Dead fields carrying fixture info the app ignores.
recommended_fix: Remove the fields and discard the tuple (_, _, _ = seed_fixture(...)), or actually use them (e.g. seed the initial view).

title: app/main.odin never calls run_destroy on its Run_State
detail: run_init allocates the topology arrays, action_log and events; the app defers only catalogs_destroy. The Run_State buffers leak at window close (process exit reclaims them, so impact is cosmetic).
recommended_fix: Add `defer pp.run_destroy(&app.state)` beside the catalogs_destroy defer.

title: load_catalogs is duplicated verbatim in app/main.odin and harness/catalogs.odin
detail: Two byte-identical copies of the catalog-loading proc in two packages. When 1.3 adds packet/demand catalogs, one copy will be updated and the other missed, silently diverging app vs harness catalog hashes.
recommended_fix: Share one implementation (core-owned bytes-to-Catalogs helper or a small shared package) instead of copying.
